newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian hostage dies in escape attempt - guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: Indian hostage dies in escape attempt - guerrillas.

text.p: Separatist guerrillas in northeast India said on Wednesday that an aid worker they captured last month had died falling from a cliff while trying to escape.
The United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) said in a statement that Sanjoy Ghosh died on Monday in a remote mountainous area of Arunachal Pradesh state, close to India's border with China.

"As we were making arrangements for his release he tried to escape and slipped from a cliff," the statement quoted ULFA spokesman Mithinga Daimari as saying. "It was a small mistake on his part which cost him his life."
Maoist ULFA kidnapped Ghosh in Majuli islands on July 4, suspecting him to be an intelligence agent.
Police and intelligence officials in the state believe Ghosh was killed immediately after his kidnapping.

But a senior military officer in the neighbouring state of Assam, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters: "Our intelligence unit has intercepted two radio messages, confirming his death in ULFA's custody on Monday evening.

"The first radio message by a top ULFA guerrilla leader to his colleagues said Sanjoy Ghosh died while he tried to escape jumping from a highland in the mountainous state of Arunachal Pradesh," the officer said.

"The second message, by another guerrilla, directed the publicity unit of the outfit to issue a press statement on Tuesday saying Sanjoy died in an encounter between them and military in the same area," he added.
The ULFA statement gave no information on Ghosh's body, which security forces have yet to recover.
Amnesty International and several Indian social organisations had appealed to ULFA for Ghosh's release.
ULFA is one of several groups fighting for independent homelands in the north east of India. The region has been racked by separatist violence for decades.
